13.14.3. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<op_code>

Number

Allowed values:

  • 34: configures local RRC release timer

  • 46: configures the user DRX cycle

  • 75: configures TAU after local RRC release

  • 101: configures the UE-specific DRX cycle

  • 104: configures the HPPLMN search

<param_val>

Number

Supported content depends on related <op_code>.

<op_code> 34

<local_rrc_inactivity_timer>

Number

This cellular platform specific guard timer is restarted with each received or transmitted packet. Set in seconds, it causes a local RRC connection release upon expiry. This feature can be used to ensure timely RRC connection release within a defined maximum delay.

The factory-programmed value is 0, which means the feature is disabled. Value changes are applied runtime.

Behavior after the local RRC connection release is specified by +MEDCR <op_code>=75.

<op_code> 46

<UserDrxCycle>

Number

Selects the idle mode DRX cycle used by the UE in a network un-coordinated way.

Monitoring fewer paging occasions than the network-configured ones lowers power consumption when no MT data is expected or when in static conditions, if the network implements a paging retransmission strategy. Otherwise it can lead to paging loss.

Allowed values:

  • 1 (factory-programmed value): feature disabled, the UE uses the network default DRX cycle.

  • (2, 4, 8): the UE monitors paging with the network default DRX cycle * <UserDrxCycle> factor periodicity. Do not use factors leading to user DRX cycles larger than 2560 ms.

Runtime changes are not supported. Use a +CFUN=0/+CFUN=1 cycle to apply the setting.

<op_code> 75

<local_rrc_release_tau>

Number

Defines the behavior after a local RRC connection release, as a consequence of local RRC inactivity timer (see <op_code>=34) expiry or local RRC connection release trigger (*FASTDORM).

Value changes are applied runtime. Allowed values:

  • 0 (factory-programmed value): initiate a TAU of type "combined TA/LA updating"

  • 1: do not initiate a TAU

  • 2: initiate a TAU of type "combined TA/LA updating with IMSI attach"

  • 3: initiate a TAU of type "periodic updating"

<op_code> 101

<UeSpecificDrxCycle>

Number

Allows to select an idle mode DRX cycle shorter than the network default one, in a network-coordinated manner.

A shorter DRX cycle improves synchronization in challenging network conditions and reduces MT data latency.

Allowed values:

  • (0,16): feature disabled, the UE uses the network default DRX cycle. The factory-programmed value is 0.

  • (6-9): during the registration procedure the UE signals the selected <UeSpecificDrxCycle> value to the network.The network and the UE use selected value only if shorter than the network defaut DRX cycle. Allowed values follow:

    • 6: 320 ms

    • 7: 640 ms

    • 8: 1280 ms

    • 9: 2560 ms

Runtime changes are not supported. Use a +CFUN=0/+CFUN=1 cycle to apply the setting.

The network and the UE always use the same DRX cycle. In case eDRX is used with <Assigned_eDRX_cycle_value> of "0000", i.e. 5120 ms (see +CEDRXRDP), a 5120 ms paging cycle is used with any DRX and <Assigned_paging_time_window> settings.

<op_code> 104

<hpplmn_timer>

Number

Configures the periodic background search for higher priority PLMN (HPPLMN).

Allowed values:

  • 0: SIM configuration EFHPPLMN is used (see the 3GPP TS 31.102 [11] subclause 4.2.6)

  • (1-80): HPPLMN search is performed with 6 minutes * <hpplmn_timer> periodicity. Initial HPPLMN search timer value is 2min.

  • 255: HPPLMN search disabled

Runtime changes are not supported. Use a +CFUN=0/+CFUN=1 cycle to apply the setting.

14. Power management

14.1. Power saving control (Power SaVing) +UPSV

+UPSV

Modules

All products

Attributes

Syntax

PIN required

Settings saved

Can be aborted

Response time

Error reference

Partial

No

NVM

No

-

+CME Error

14.1.1. Description

Sets the UART power saving configuration, but it has a global effect on the module power saving configuration. When the power saving is enabled, the module automatically enters the low power idle mode whenever possible, reducing the power consumption.

  • If the power saving is disabled (+UPSV: 0), the UART interface is always enabled and the module is not allowed to enter the low power idle mode.

  • When power saving is enabled using <mode>=1, the UART interface is disabled and the module enters the low power idle mode as soon as possible. To re-enable the UART and wake up the module from sleep it is necessary to send a character on the UART interface; the character is lost.

  • When power saving is enabled using <mode>=3, the UART interface is enabled and the module does not enter the low power idle mode as long as the UART DTR line (or a specific GPIO, see <GPIO_mode>=34, in +UGPIOC AT command) is high.

14.1.2. Syntax

Type Syntax Response Example

Generic syntax

Set

AT+UPSV=<mode>

OK

AT+UPSV=0

OK

Power saving disabling

Set

AT+UPSV=0

OK

AT+UPSV=0

OK

Power saving controlled by the UART RX line

Set

AT+UPSV=1

OK

AT+UPSV=1

OK

Power saving controlled by the UART DTR line

Set

AT+UPSV=3

OK

AT+UPSV=3

OK

+UPSV: <mode>

OK

+UPSV: 0

OK

OK

+UPSV: (0,1,3)

OK

14.1.3. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<mode>

Number

Power saving configurations:

  • 0: (default and factory-programmed value): power saving disabled.

  • 1: UART is immediately disabled and the module power saving is automatically entered when conditions allow it.

    • Data reception from the host (first character is lost) re-enables the UART and power saving is immediately disabled.

    • If UART is enabled and power saving exited, <mode>=1 has to be re-issued to enable power saving again.

<mode>=1 is not persistent

  • 3: power saving is controlled by UART DTR (or specific GPIO) line:

    • if the DTR line (or specific GPIO) state is set to OFF, the power saving is allowed

    • if the DTR line (or specific GPIO) state is set to ON, the module shall exit from power saving, unless it has already entered the deep-sleep mode

<mode>=3 is allowed regardless of the flow control setting on the UART interface. In particular, the HW flow control can be set on UART during this mode.

<mode>=3 is allowed in 2 UARTs configuration only by using a specific GPIO with <GPIO_mode>=34

With <mode>=3 the DTE can start sending data to the module without risk of data loss after having asserted the UART DTR line or the specific GPIO (DTR line/GPIO set to ON state).

14.1.4. Notes

  • The UART CTS line is just related to HW flow control and cannot be used by the host to monitor the UART power saving state (it doesn’t switch to OFF state when power saving is entered); hence, the host has to keep track of UART power saving state based on +UPSV AT command usage (in <mode>=1) or DTR line state (in <mode>=3).

  • In <mode>=1, the UART is immediately disabled but UART wakes-up for URCs sending to host are still guaranteed and are automatic.

  • In <mode>=1 and with UART disabled, it is recommended to send "AT" or "at" followed by the line termination character multiple times as wake-up commands, until an "OK" is received, before proceeding with the requested AT commands.

  • In <mode>=1, upon a wake-up from sleep (via a character sent to the module) and with the UART enabled again, it is necessary to re-issue the AT+UPSV=1 command to re-arm the UART power saving and allow the module entering into the low power idle mode. Hence, the <mode>=1 has to be used by the host when it has completed its AT commands session to allow the module sleep. Whenever a new interaction is requested, the host shall re-enable the UART in the described way.

  • In <mode>=1 and in case of +USIO: 1, both UARTs are synchronously enabled or disabled and the UARTs wake up upon data received over one of the 2 interfaces.

  • In <mode>=3, if the UART DTR (or the configured GPIO, in a mutually exclusive way) is high, the UART interface is enabled and the module does not enter the low power idle mode; then, when the UART DTR (or the configured GPIO, in a mutually exclusive way) gets low, the module enters the low power idle mode as soon as possible and the UART interface is disabled.

  • In <mode>=3, the setting of <GPIO_mode>=34 for either GPIO3 or GPIO6 automatically moves the power saving control logic from the UART DTR line to the GPIO.

  • In the 2 UARTs configuration (+USIO: 1 or +USIO: 5 configuration) <mode>=3 is only allowed if the GPIO3 or GPIO6 is configured for power saving control (see <GPIO_mode>=34, in +UGPIOC AT command), since the UART DTR line is not available.

  • Regardless of the set <mode>, if the USB is present and not suspended, UARTs are always enabled and the module cannot enter the the low power idle mode.

  • PSM deep-sleep mode configuration is independent from the low power idle mode configuration and it is not controlled by this AT command.

14.2. Power Saving Mode Setting +CPSMS

+CPSMS

Modules

All products

Attributes

Syntax

PIN required

Settings saved

Can be aborted

Response time

Error reference

Partial

Yes

NVM / OP

No

< 10 s

+CME Error

14.2.1. Description

Controls the setting of the UEs Power Saving Mode (PSM) parameters. The command controls whether the UE wants to apply PSM or not, as well as:

  • The requested extended periodic RAU value in GERAN/UTRAN

  • The requested GPRS READY timer value in GERAN/UTRAN

  • The requested extended periodic TAU value in E-UTRAN

  • The requested Active Time value in E-UTRAN.

The +CPSMS <mode> parameter defines whether the Power Saving Mode (PSM) feature usage is requested to the network.

  • If Power Saving Mode (PSM) is requested (+CPSMS: 1) and granted by the network, i.e. Active Time has been assigned, PSM deep-sleep can be entered: after the expiry of the assigned Active Time (T3324) every SW and HW component on the device powers down except for the real time clock (RTC). The module stays powered down until the expiry of the assigned extended periodic TAU value (T3412_ext) or the assigned periodic TAU value (T3412) (if the former has not been assigned) or an early wake-up event (which consists in a proper toggling of the PWR_ON input line).

  • Per 3GPP it is not possible to negotiate an T3412_ext timer without specifying a valid Active Time (T3324). The opposite is allowed.

  • PSM deep-sleep is not entered if PSM is disabled (+CPSMS: 0) or not granted by the network.

  • PSM can be configured runtime, in which case a TAU is performed, and in minimum functionality (even with SIM disabled or not inserted).

The command settings shall be changed in deregistered state, i.e. in minimum functionality mode (+CFUN: 0) or in airplane mode (+CFUN: 4).

If the set command is issued and an optional parameter is omitted, the module applies the last set value.

14.2.2. Syntax

Type Syntax Response Example

Set

AT+CPSMS=[<mode>[,<Requested_Periodic_RAU>[,<Requested_GPRS_READY_timer>[,<Requested_Periodic_TAU>,[<Requested_Active_Time>]]]]]

OK

AT+CPSMS=1,,,"01000011","01000011"

OK

Read

AT+CPSMS?

+CPSMS: <mode>,[<Requested_Periodic_RAU>],[<Requested_GPRS_READY_timer>],[<Requested_Periodic_TAU>],[<Requested_Active_Time>]

OK

+CPSMS: 1,,,"01000011","01000011"

OK

Test

AT+CPSMS=?

+CPSMS: (list of supported <mode>s),(list of supported <Requested_Periodic_RAU>s),(list of supported <Requested_GPRS_READY_timer>s),(list of supported <Requested_Periodic_TAU>s),(list of supported <Requested_Active_Time>s)

OK

+CPSMS: (0,1,2),,,("00000000"-"11111111"),("00000000"-"11111111")

OK

14.2.3. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<mode>

Number

Indication to disable or enable the use of PSM in the UE. Allowed values:

  • 0 (default value): disable the use of PSM

  • 1: enable the use of PSM

  • 2: disable the use of PSM and reset all parameters for PSM to factory-programmed values.

Factory-programmed value:

  • 0

<Requested_Periodic_RAU>

String

One byte in an 8 bit format. Requested extended periodic RAU value (T3312_ext) to be allocated to the UE in GERAN/UTRAN. The requested extended periodic RAU value is coded as one byte (octet 3) of the GPRS Timer 3 information element coded as bit format (e.g. "01000111" equals 70 hours). For the coding and the value range, see the GPRS Timer 3 IE in 3GPP TS 24.008 table 10.5.163a/3GPP TS 24.008 [8]. See also 3GPP TS 23.682 [8]. See also 3GPP TS 23.682 [44] and 3GPP TS 23.060 [35]. The factory-programmed value is:

  • The parameter is not supported.

<Requested_GPRS_READY_timer>

String

One byte in an 8 bit format. Requested GPRS READY timer value (T3314) to be allocated to the UE in GERAN/UTRAN. The requested GPRS READY timer value is coded as one byte (octet 2) of the GPRS Timer information element coded as bit format (e.g. "01000011" equals 3 decihours or 18 minutes). For the coding and the value range, see the GPRS Timer IE in 3GPP TS 24.008 table 10.5.172/3GPP TS 24.008 [8]. See also 3GPP TS 23.060 [35]. The factory-programmed value is:

  • The parameter is not supported.

<Requested_Periodic_TAU>

String

One byte in an 8 bit format. Requested extended periodic TAU value (T3412_ext) to be allocated to the UE in E-UTRAN. The requested extended periodic TAU value is coded as one byte (octet 3) of the GPRS Timer 3 information element coded as bit format (e.g. "01000111" equals 70 hours). For the coding and value range, see the GPRS Timer 3 IE in 3GPP TS 24.008 table 10.5.163a/3GPP TS 24.008 [8]. See also 3GPP TS 23.682 [44] and 3GPP TS 23.401 [45].

  • The default and factory-programmed value is "00000001" (10 minutes).

<Requested_Active_Time>

String

One byte in an 8 bit format. Requested Active Time value (T3324) to be allocated to the UE in GERAN/UTRAN or in EUTRAN. The requested Active Time value is coded as one byte (octet 3) of the GPRS Timer 2 information element coded as bit format (e.g. "00100100" equals 4 minutes). For the coding and value range, see the GPRS Timer 2 IE in 3GPP TS 24.008 table 10.5.163/3GPP TS 24.008 [8]. See also 3GPP TS 23.682 [44], 3GPP TS 23.060 [35] and 3GPP TS 23.401 [45].

  • The default and factory-programmed value is "00011110" (30 seconds).

14.2.4. Notes

  • To enter PSM deep-sleep mode, enable both PSM and deep-sleep (see +SCCFG).

  • When in PSM, +CREG, +CEREG, +CELLINFO, +CNETCI, +CSQ, +CESQ, +SIGNS and +UCGED diagnostic AT commands return information gathered before entering PSM, with the exception of the <RSRQ>, <RSRP>, <RSSI>, and <RSSNR> parameters reported by +UCGED.

  • <mode>=2 behaves like <mode>=0.

  • The <mode> parameter is mandatory.

  • The PIN insertion is not mandatory before the command execution.

  • The <Requested_Periodic_RAU> and <Requested_GPRS_READY_timer> parameters are ignored when configured in the set command. They are reported with "" values in the read command response.

  • The test command response is +CPSMS: (0-2).

15. GPIO

15.1. Introduction

The section describes the AT commands used to configure the GPIO pins provided by cellular modules.

15.1.1. GPIO functions

On cellular modules, GPIO pins can be opportunely configured as general purpose input or output. Moreover GPIO pins of cellular modules can be configured to provide custom functions via +UGPIOC AT command. 15.1.3. Network status indication

When a GPIO pin is configured to provide network status indication, its progress depends on the network registration state (see +CEREG) and on the module transmission state:

  • No service: indicates no network coverage or not registered state

  • Registered home network 2G: indicates registered state on home network in 2G RAT

  • Registered home network 3G: indicates registered state on home network in 3G RAT

  • Registered home network 4G: indicates registered state on home network in 4G RAT

  • Registered home network NB-IoT: indicates registered state on home network in NB-IoT

  • Registered roaming 2G: indicates registered state with visitor 2G network (roaming in 2G RAT)

  • Registered roaming 3G: indicates registered state with visitor 3G network (roaming in 3G RAT)

  • Registered roaming 4G: indicates registered state with visitor 4G network (roaming in 4G RAT)

  • Registered roaming NB-IoT: indicates registered state with visitor NB-IoT network (roaming in NB-IoT)

  • Data transmission: indicates voice or data call active either in 2G, 3G or 4G RAT

  • Data transmission roaming: indicates voice or data call active either in 2G, 3G or 4G RAT with visitor network

The following figures report the allowed progresses for GPIO pin set as network indication: VH and VL values are provided in the corresponding module data sheet in the "Generic Digital Interfaces pins" section.

15.1.4. UART (DSR, DTR, DCD e RI) interface

The UART interface lines (DSR, DTR, DCD and RI) can be set on GPIO pins. For more details, see the corresponding module system integration manual.

15.1.5. Module status indication

When a GPIO pin is configured to provide module status indication, its progress depends on the current module status (power-off mode, i.e. module switched off, or deep-sleep mode versus idle, active or connected mode, i.e. module switched on):

  • Output / High, when the module is switched on (any operating mode during module normal operation: idle, active or connected mode)

  • Output / Low, when the module is switched off (power-off mode)

15.1.6. Module operating mode indication

When a GPIO pin is configured to provide module operating mode indication, its progress depends on the current module operating mode (the low power idle mode versus active or connected mode):

  • Output / High, when the module is in active or connected mode

  • Output / Low, when the module is in idle mode (that can be reached if the power saving is enabled by the +UPSV AT command)

15.2. GPIO select configuration command +UGPIOC

+UGPIOC

Modules

15.2.1. Description

Configures the GPIO pins as input, output, or to handle a custom function. When a GPIO pin is configured as an output pin (<gpio_mode>=0), it is possible to set the output value <gpio_out_val> which will be returned in the information text response to +UGPIOR read command (where supported). When a GPIO pin is configured as an input pin (<gpio_mode>=1), it is possible to set the input value <gpio_in_pull> which will be returned in the information text response to +UGPIOR read command (where supported). When the GPIO pin is configured as a SIM card detection (<gpio_mode>=7), it is possible to set the SIM polarity <gpio_sim_det_logic>; the parameter setting will be returned in the information text response to +UGPIOC read command.

The test command provides the list of the supported GPIOs, the supported functions and the status of all the GPIOs.

Not all the GPIO functions can be assigned to each GPIO pin. If the configuration is not allowed, an error result code will be returned (error result code 1502 - "+CME ERROR: Select GPIO mode error"). Where supported, the following custom functions cannot be simultaneously configured on 2 GPIOs:

  • Network status indication

  • External GNSS supply enable

  • External GNSS data ready

  • External GNSS RTC sharing

  • Jamming detection indication

  • Headset detection

  • GSM Tx burst indication

  • Module status indication

  • Module operating mode indication

  • Ring indicator

  • Last gasp

  • External GNSS antenna / LNA control

  • Time pulse GNSS

  • Time pulse output

  • Time stamp of external interrupt

  • Fast power-off

  • External GNSS time pulse input

  • External GNSS time stamp of external interrupt

  • DTR mode for power saving control

  • 32.768 kHz output

  • Safe memory and power-off

  • UPSV control

  • Primary UART DTR line on GPIO pin

  • GNSS Rx indication

  • GNSS Rx/Tx indication

When assigning one of these functionalities on a second pin, the previous pin will be automatically set to "Pin disabled" mode (255), except for the "UPSV control" functionality (34) where this operation will return an ERROR.

For more details regarding the custom functions supported by the cellular modules and the factory-programmed settings, see GPIO functions and GPIO mapping.

Number

15.2.4. Notes

  • <gpio_sim_det_logic> is not supported.

  • The network status indication (<gpio_mode>=2) and ring indicator function (<gpio_mode>=18) can be set on every pin except GPIO3 and GPIO6.

  • The module status indication function (<gpio_mode>=10) can be set on GPIO2 and GPIO4 only.

  • The SIM card detection function (<gpio_mode>=7) works only at run-time; hence the command shall be issued at each boot.

  • To switch the GPIO functionality from "SIM card detection" feature to another one, firstly set the pin as "Pin disabled" (<gpio_mode>=255). After that the pin can be configured with the desired GPIO functionality.

16.2.1. Description

Opens a file in USER file system with the specified name filename parameter, returning its handle that can be used for future read/write operations.

The returned handle can be disassociated from the file by calling AT+FCLOSE.

File should be considered a stream: once opened, the position indicator (internal pointer) points to the beginning of the file. Each following read/write activity will change the position affecting the point from where the next command applies.

16.2.2. Syntax

<mode>

Number

Allowed values are:

  • 0 (default value): if the file does not exist, a new file is created; if the file exists, open the file directly. The files in both cases are readable and writable.

  • 1: if the file does not exist, a new file is created; if the file exists, the file is cleared and overwritten. The files in both cases are readable and writable.

  • 2: if the file exists, it opens the file and the file is only readable; if the file does not exist, an error is returned.

16.11. File system limits

16.11.1. Allowed characters in filenames and folders name

A filename cannot:

  • contain one of the following characters: \ / : * ? " < > |

  • begin with "." or "blank".

  • end with "."

Character "\" must be used only as separator between names of folders and files when using File System paths.

16.11.2. Limits

See below the maximum filename length, the maximum data size of the file system, and the maximum number of files for the cellular modules.

Maximum filename length:

  • 115 characters

Maximum file size:

  • File size limited by the available file system space retrieved by AT+ULSTFILE command. The file system space could change during the time, even if it is not directly used by the customer’s application.

Maximum number of files:

  • There is no limit to the number of files that can be stored besides the available file system space retrieved by AT+ULSTFILE command. Consider that up to 4 kB can be used by the file system driver to properly store each file.

The theoretical maximum file size and the maximum number of files that can be stored in the file system are affected by the metadata needed to properly store the files, and by system, hidden and temporary files whose number is not statically predictable, so the actual numbers can be lower than stated.

17.2.1. Description

Configures the primary and/or the secondary DNS (Domain Name Server). The default DNS configuration is provided by the network via PCO (Protocol Configuration Options) during LTE attach. The user defined DNS shall be configured after the activaton of the socket service (with +NETOPEN AT command) or the IP application session (e.g. with +UHTTPSTART AT command). Restarting the socket service or the application session restores the default DNS configuration.

The modified configuration is effective only on the default CID (<cid>= 1); for different CIDs the default DNS is used.

If the module is not registered to any network, the read command returns ERROR.

18. Internet protocol transport layer

18.1. Introduction

TCP and UDP sockets are independently and simultaneously managed via dedicated AT commands over the same EPS bearer/PDP context. AT commands for both reading and writing data on sockets are provided, and incoming data and transmission result are notified to the external application via URCs, therefore polling is not needed.

Before using TCP/IP services, a connection profile must be defined. See +CGDCONT AT commands for configuring a PDP context.

If not specified the default CID (<cid>=1) is used.

The UDP protocol has no flow control mechanism and uplink packets might be lost in the following scenarios:

  • No network signal is available

  • Unreliable radio interface (e.g. mobility with radio link failures, which can lead to data loss, that in GPRS can be contrasted with the usage of LLC ack reliability QoS parameter)

Some network operators close dynamic NATs after few minutes if there is no activity on the connection (no data transfer in the period). To solve this problem enable the TCP keep alive option with 1 minute delay (see the +USHBT AT command).

When both TCP and UDP sockets are used at the same time at the maximum throughput (downlink and uplink at the maximum allowed baud rate) it is possible to lose some incoming UDP packets due to internal buffer limitation. A possible workaround is provided as follows:

  • If it is possible, adopt an application layer UDP acknowledge system

18.1.1. <socket>

The <socket> parameter sets the socket identifier to be used for any future operation on that socket. <socket> range lists the allowed range:

Table 14. <socket> range
Product Maximum number of sockets Allowed range

ADAM-R11

10

0-9

18.2. IPv4/IPv6 addressing

18.2.1. Introduction

The section describes the IP addressing formats and IP address rules used by TCP/IP UDP/IP enabled applications.

18.2.2. IPv4

Format:

  • 32 bits long in dot-decimal notation (without leading 0 notation).

  • All the decimal numbers must be in range 0-255.

  • The dot-octal notation is not supported.

  • The dot-hexadecimal notation is not supported.

Examples:

Table 15. IPv4 address format examples
IPv4 address Remarks

254.254.254.254

Valid address

010.228.76.34

Invalid address; first decimal number prefixed with a leading zero

257.228.76.34

Invalid address; first decimal number greater than 255

0010.0344.0114.0042

Invalid address; dot-octal notation; decimals given as octal numbers

0x10.0xE4.0x4C.0x22

Invalid address; dot-hexadecimal notation; decimals given as hexadecimal numbers

18.3. Start socket service +NETOPEN

+NETOPEN

18.3.1. Description

Starts the socket service by activating the default PDP context. The command must be performed before executing any other TCP/UDP related operation. A specific PDP context can be activated providing the <cid> parameter.

If the PDP context is closed for a network error (e.g. Out of Service) the +CIPEVENT URC is provided. When this event happens, the user needs to check and close all opened sockets, and then uses the AT+NETCLOSE command to release the PDP context if AT+NETOPEN? shows the network is still opened. If the AT+NETOPEN=<cid> command was used to activate a PDP context, it is notified an independent URC reporting the <cid> parameter for each activated PDP context.

The maximum response time can be configured by setting the <netopen_timeout> parameter of the +USTO AT command.

The default PDP context activated by starting the socket service can be configured with the +USPDP AT command.

Type Syntax Response Example

AT+NETOPEN

[OK|ERROR]

AT+NETOPEN

[OK|ERROR]

AT+NETOPEN

18.3.3. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<cid>

Number

Specifies the PDP context to be activated. For the parameter range, see <cid>.

For more details on the default value of the parameter (where supported), see Internet protocol transport layer.

<net_state>

Number

Indicates the state of the PDP context activation:

  • 0: network close (deactivated)

  • 1: network open (activated)

<err>

Number

The result of operation:

  • 0: action successful

  • Different values mean an unsuccessful action; allowed value are listed in the TCP/UDP/IP stack error codes table.

<err_info>

Number or string

Error code causing the failure:

  • 4: Network is already opened

The value format (numeric or string) of the error result code can be changed by the +USCFG AT command.

18.3.4. Notes

  • The command returns ERROR with the IRC specifying the error code, if the PDP context has already been activated.

18.6.1. Description

Sets the default PDP context profile and the IP type of the socket service. The profile parameters can be configured by the AT+CGDCONT command.

The value of the <ip_family> parameter determines the default address family of all sockets as reported by the +USIPCFG AT command querying the IP family type of a socket.

18.6.4. Note

  • To take effect, the command must be sent before starting the socket service, otherwise it will fail.

  • The value of the <ip_family> parameter must comply with the IP type of the PDP context set by the AT command +CGDCONT; by setting it to 1 (IPv4) or 6 (IPv6) while the PDP context is only IPv4 or IPv6 respectively, the AT command to connect a socket (+USOPEN) will fail.

<err_info>

  • 8: Network not opened

The value format (numeric or string) of the error result code can be changed by the +USCFG AT command.

18.7.4. Notes

  • The action command returns the IP address type of the active PDP context based on the value of the parameter <ip_family> of the +USPDP AT command.

  • The set command returns all the IP addresses of the active PDP context identified by the <cid> value.

+USOPEN

18.8.1. Description

Establishes a connection with the specified remote host peer on the given remote port, like the BSD connect routine. If the socket is a TCP socket, the command will actually perform the TCP negotiation (3-way handshake) to open a connection. If the socket is a UDP socket, this function merely reserves the local port to be used to communicate with the remote peer.

Socket service must be already started by the +NETOPEN.

The <socket> value is restricted to be only 0 if the direct link mode is enabled.

The maximum response time can be configured by setting the <usopen_timeout> parameter of the +USTO AT command.

18.10. Send socket data +USSEND

+USSEND

Modules

18.10.1. Description

Sends data to a remote host through a TCP or UDP connection. The command returns the ‘>’ character indicating the start of the data entry to be sent.

If the <length> field is not specified, data received on the COM port will be sent to the remote host. The <Ctrl+Z> character terminates data entry and trigger data sending; the <ESC> character aborts data sending.
To send the <Ctrl+Z> or <ESC> character, they must be encoded as <ETX><Ctrl+Z> or <ETX><ESC>. To send the character <ETX> it must be encoded as <ETX><ETX>.
<ETX> is 0x03, <Ctrl+Z> is 0x1A and <ESC> is 0x1B.

Socket service must be already started by the +NETOPEN.

Both the <remote_addr> and <remote_port> parameters are mandatory for UDP sockets.

Command can be aborted only if length is not specified.

The maximum response time can be configured by setting the <usopen_timeout> parameter of the +USTO AT command.

18.10.3. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<socket>

Number

The socket through which to send data; see <socket>.

Valid range is 0-9.

<length>

Number

Number of data bytes to send

Range is 1-1500

<remote_addr>

String

IP address or domain name of the remote host. For IP address format reference see the IP addressing.

The parameter is mandatory for a UDP socket.

<remote_port>

Number

Remote host port, in range 1-65535

The parameter is mandatory for a UDP socket.

<data>

String

Data bytes to be sent.

<reqSendLength>

Number

The length of data requested to be sent.

<cnfSendLength>

Number

The length of data confirmed to have been sent:

  • -1: the connection is closed

  • 0: internal buffer or congestion windows are full

  • >0: data bytes sent

If the value <cnfSendLength> is different from the value <reqSendLength>, the socket can no longer be used.

<err>

Number

The result of operation

  • 0: action successful

  • Different values mean an unsuccessful action; allowed value are listed in the TCP/UDP/IP stack error codes table.

18.10.4. Notes

  • For a TCP connection, the data is buffered into the internal TCP/IP stack and then sent to the remote host by the protocol stack.
    The URC is triggered according to the setting of the +USSENDCFG AT command.

  • Refer to the +USSTAT AT command to check the TCP socket status and pending acknowledgements after sending data, if you need to strictly control the data sent over the network and received by the remote peer.

  • Sending over a UDP connection a packet of bytes larger than 1400 may result in the server not receiving the data due to network operator limitations.

18.13. Receive data socket +USGET

18.13.1. Description

The command allows selecting the received data handling mode between Buffer Access mode and Direct Push mode.

In Direct Push mode (<mode>=0) the data from remote host is directly outputted to the AT terminal by an URC with the indication of the address and port of the sender and the data length.
In Buffer Access mode (<mode>=1) the received data are buffered notifying the host by an URC.

The command can also be used to obtain the amount of buffered data (<mode>=4) and to retrieve a specific number of bytes (<mode>=2 and <mode>=3) from the buffer.

Socket service must be already started by the AT+NETOPEN command and the connection established by the AT+USOPEN command.

Setting <mode>=0 or <mode>=1 has no effect if the socket is already connected.

In Direct Push mode the URC composition can be modified including or not the IP header (+IPD<data length>) by the +USHDR AT command and the remote IP address and port (+RECV FROM: <remote_addr>,<remote_port>) by the AT+USINFO command.

Parameter Type Description

<mode>

Number

Set the mode to retrieve the received data:

  • 0: (default value) received data are managed in Push Direct mode

  • 1: received data are managed in Buffer Access mode

  • 2: read data

  • 3: read data in HEX format

  • 4: retrieve the number of bytes in the buffer

Max value is:

<remote_addr>

Number

The length of data confirmed to have been sent:

  • -1: the connection is closed

  • 0: internal buffer or congestion windows are full

  • >0: number of bytes sent

If the value <cnfSendLength> is different from the value <reqSendLength>, the socket can no longer be used.

<err_info>

Number

Error code causing the failure. Refer to the error info table.

The value format (numeric or string) of the error result code can be changed by the +USCFG AT command.

18.13.4. Notes

  • For a closed socket, unread bytes in the receive buffer can still be retrieved until the same socket is reconnected.

  • In case data is received after a no service condition (e.g. +CEREG: 2), the "data received" URC might be lost; it is therefore recommended to periodically query the amount of buffered data.

18.16. Set Direct Link mode for socket service +USMODE

+USMODE

Modules

All products

Attributes

Syntax

PIN required

Settings saved

Can be aborted

Response time

Error reference

Full

No

No

No

9 s

-

18.16.1. Description

Establishes a transparent end-to-end communication when connecting a TCP or UDP socket to a remote host via the serial interface. The data can be sent to the socket and can be received via the serial interface: the HW flow control usage is strongly recommended to avoid data loss.

The transparent TCP/UDP connection mode can be exited via the +++ sequence or via the DTR line transition according the &D configuration. The socket will remain connected and communication can be re-established any time by the ATO command.

The Direct Link mode can be established only for one socket at the time, either TCP client or TCP server. The first server (<server_index>=0) and the first client socket (<socket>=0) are used for transparent mode operation; other servers (<server_index>=1-3) and other client sockets (<socket>=1-9) cannot be used.

Any incoming data is buffered in the internal TCP/IP protocol stack after exiting from the Direct Link mode and will be reported when the transparent connection is re-established.

The sequence <CR><LF>CLOSED<CR><LF> is provided by deactivating the PDP context for the socket service (+NETCLOSE), by locally closing the socket (+USCLOSE), the remote peer closes the connection or for abnormal network state (e.g. a failed registration due to mobility) when the connection for the <socket>=0 is established in Direct Link mode.

Escape sequence +++ is detected when it is received by the module in a single separate frame of 3 bytes length. The escape sequence will not be recognized if the time interval between each character is greater than 900 milliseconds. To avoid missed detection of the escape sequence, it is suggested to send +++ when the COM port has CTS asserted/flow control disabled.

OK

+USMODE: 1

OK

Test

+USMODE: (list of supported <mode>s)

OK

+USMODE=?

+USMODE: (0-1)

OK

18.16.3. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<mode>

Number

Direct Link mode:

  • 0: (default value) disabled

  • 1: enabled

18.16.4. Notes

  • The configuration of the Direct Link mode must be done before starting the socket service by the +NETOPEN AT command, otherwise the +USMODE will respond with ERROR.

Sets the mode the <err_info> (refer to the table) is reported:

  • 0: error result code is reported as a numeric value

  • 1: (default value) error result code is reported as a string value

<HeaderType>

Number

Specifies the string format to report the receiving of data:

  • 0: (default value) the format is "+IPD<data length>"

  • 1: the format is "+RECEIVE,<link num>,<data length>"

<AsyncMode>

Number

Reserved

The parameter is present to be compatible with old TCP/IP commands set.

<TimeoutVal>

Number

Set the minimum retransmission timeout value in milliseconds for a TCP connection.

The allowed range is 500-120000 ms.

The default value is 500.

18.21. Socket control parameters +USDS

+USDS

Modules

All products

Attributes

Syntax

PIN required

Settings saved

Can be aborted

Response time

Error reference

Full

No

No

No

9 s

-

18.21.1. Description

Sets specific control parameters of the socket.

  • TCP SYN packet re-transmission backoff: sets the number of attempts and the interval between them used by the TCP/IP protocol stack to establish a connection with a remote host.

The first SYN packet re-transmission always occurs 3 seconds after the initial attempt; this behaviour cannot be suppressed or modified.

  • TCP data packet re-transmission backoff: sets the number of attempts and the interval between them used by the TCP/IP protocol stack to send a data packet before receiving the ACK from the remote host.

The first data packet re-transmission always occurs 1 seconds after the initial attempt; this behaviour cannot be suppressed or modified.

  • Maximum transmission unit: sets the size of the largest data unit can be sent over the data connection without fragmentation.

  • Receive window size: sets the size of the receive window; this value is used in the TCP connection handshake to notify the remote peer how much data it is willing to accept.

  • Send window size: sets the maximum number of bytes that TCP/IP’s internal buffer can handle while waiting for them to be correctly sent.

  • DNS retries backoff: configures the maximum number of attempts and the interval between them used by the DNS client to obtain an IP address.

By setting the <dns_wait_tmr> parameter with less than 2 items or its first element to a value of less than 2 seconds, the behaviour of the device in resolving a hostname becomes unpredictable.

18.21.2. Syntax

Type Syntax Response Example

Generic syntax

Set

AT+USDS=<op_code>,<param>

[OK|ERROR]

AT+USDS="Tcp srxt",6

OK

Read

+USDS: "Tcp rxt",<rtx>,<tcp_backoff>

+USDS: "Mtu",<mtu>

+USDS: "RecvWin",<rwin>

+USDS: "DnsTmr",<dnsMaxWaitTime>,<dnsMaxRetry>,<dns_wait_tmr>

+USDS: "SendWin",<swin>

OK

+USDS: "RecvWin",64240

+USDS: "DnsTmr",4,1,4,3,4,8,8,8,8,8

+USDS: "SendWin",64240

OK

18.21.3. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<op_code>

String

Control parameter to set; it identifies the meaning of the next parameter(s).

Allowed values are:

  • "Tcp srxt": TCP SYN re-transmission backoff

  • "Tcp rxt": TCP data packet re-transmission backoff

  • "Mtu": Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) size

  • "RecvWin": Receive window size

  • "DnsTmr": DNS retries backoff

  • "SendWin": Send window size

<srxt>

Number

Maximum number of TCP SYN packets retransmitted.

The range is 1-12.

The default value is 6.

The parameter value is derived from the setting of the value of <tcp_sync_backoff>. It cannot be set.

<tcp_sync_backoff>

String

The TCP SYN packet retransmission interval backoff.

The string is a list of maximum 13 items separated by comma

The default value is "1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, 96, 120,120, 120"

<rxt>

Number

Maximum number of TCP data packets retransmitted.

The range is 1-12.

The default value is 6.

The parameter value is derived from the setting of the of <tcp_backoff>. It cannot be set.

<tcp_backoff>

String

The TCP data packet retransmission exponential backoff.

The string is a list of maximum 13 items separated by comma

Each item is an integer; the interval between subsequent retransmissions is calculated as 2 raised to the power of the item’s value (in seconds).

The default value is "1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7"

<mtu>

Number

The maximum transmission unit in bytes for a data packet.

The allowed range is 640-1500.

The default value is 1500. It may change depending on the settings of the network to which the module is attached.

<rwin>

Number

The TCP receive window size.

The allowed range is 1460-131070 bytes.

The default value is 64240.

<dnsMaxWaitTime>

Number

Maximum timeout in seconds for DNS resolution retries.

The default value is 4.

The parameter value is derived from the setting of the of <dns_wait_tmr>, see Notes. It cannot be set.

<dnsMaxRetry>

Number

Number of DNS resolution attempts.

The allowed range is 2-8 bytes.

The default value is 2.

The parameter value is derived from the setting of the of <dns_wait_tmr>, see Notes. It cannot be set.

<dns_wait_tmr>

String

The DNS attempts interval backoff.

The string is a list of maximum 8 items separated by comma

Each item is the interval in seconds between two consecutive DNS resolution attempts

The default value is "2, 3, 4, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8"

At least 2 items are required. The first element cannot be less than 2 seconds.

<swin>

Number

The TCP send window size.

The allowed range is 2920-65535 bytes.

The default value is 64240.

18.21.4. Notes

  • The <srxt> parameter represents the total number of TCP SYN retransmission attempts, calculated as the number of elements in the <tcp_sync_backoff> parameter plus one for the initial unconfigurable attempt. For example, if <tcp_sync_backoff> is set to "3,5,7", then <srxt> will be 4 (3 configured attempts + 1 initial attempt).

  • The <rxt> parameter represents the total number of TCP data packet retransmission attempts, calculated as the number of elements in the <tcp_backoff> parameter plus one for the initial unconfigurable attempt. For example, if <tcp_backoff> is set to "1,1,2,2", then <rxt> will be 5 (4 configured attempts + 1 initial attempt).

  • Changing the value of the <dns_wait_tmr> parameter for the DNS attempts backoff (<op_code>="DnsTmr") affects also the behaviour of the +USIPADDR AT command.

  • The <dnsMaxWaitTime> and <dnsMaxRetry> parameters reported by the read command (<op_code>=“DnsTmr”) are calculated based on the values of the <dns_wait_tmr> parameter and refer to the maximum timeout and maximum attempts for a single class request (A and AAAA) and for each DNS server queried to resolve a hostname. The first attempt is performed 1 second less than the value of the first element of the <dns_wait_tmr> array, so <dnsMaxWaitTime> is 1 second longer than the actual maximum timeout. E.g.: setting <dns_wait_tmr> to "2,4" results in a <dnsMaxWaitTime> of 6 seconds and a <dnsMaxRetry> of 2; having 3 DNS servers configured, the device will try to resolve a hostname for a maximum of 12 attempts (2 attempts for each class and each server), for a total of 30 seconds of maximum wait time: (<dnsMaxWaitTime> - 1) * 2 (class A and class AAAA queries) * 3 (DNS servers).

+USRVSTART

18.23.1. Description

Starts a TCP server listening on the IP address of the PDP context to which it is bound and on the specified local port. Incoming TCP client connection requests are automatically accepted and an unsolicited message is returned with information about the index of the newly created socket for the established connection, the server to which the request arrived and the IP address and port of the remote client.

Socket service must be already started by the +NETOPEN.

The <server> value is restricted to be only 0 if the direct link mode is enabled.

18.23.2. Syntax

Type Syntax Response Example

Generic syntax

Set

AT+USRVSTART=<local_port>,<server>[,<backlog>]

[OK|ERROR]

AT+USRVSTART=8080,0

OK

Read

AT+USRVSTART?

+USRVSTART: <server>,<local_port>

[…​]

OK

AT+USRVSTART?

+USRVSTART: 0,8080

OK

Test

AT+USRVSTART=?

+USRVSTART: (list of supported <local_port>s),(list of supported <server>s)

OK

AT+USRVSTART=?

+USRVSTART: (0-65535),(0-3)

OK

URC

+CLIENT: <socket>,<server>,<remote_addr>:<remote_port>

AT+USRVSTART=8080,0

OK

+CLIENT: 0,0,192.168.10.11:54321

Error indication

IRC

+CIPERROR: <err>

AT+USRVSTART=8080,4

+CIPERROR: 3

ERROR

18.23.3. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<local_port>

Number

The local port the server is listening to.

Valid Range is 0-65535.

<server>

Number

The TCP server to start.

Valid Range is 0-3.

<backlog>

String

The maximum length of the queue for the pending connections the TCP server can handle.

Valid Range is 1-3.

The default value is 3.

<remote_addr>

String

IP address of the remote host. For IP address format reference see the IP addressing.

<remote_port>

Number

The port number of the remote host.

<socket>

Number

The socket index created for the incoming connection; see <socket>.

Valid Range is 0-9.

<err>

Number

The result of operation:

  • 0: action successful

  • Different values mean an unsuccessful action; allowed value are listed in the TCP/UDP/IP stack error codes table.

18.23.4. Notes

  • If there is another service working in direct link mode, it is not allowed to set up a TCP server by the +USRVSTART AT command if the direct link mode for the socket service is enabled (+USMODE=1).

  • When the direct link mode is configured and a transparent connection with a TCP client is already active, the URC notification of a new incoming connection and the start of the related transparent communication, is delayed until the previous connection is closed with the "CLOSED" string signalling.

  • If all sockets are in use, the new incoming connections are queued in the listening queue and the TCP/IP protocol handshake is finalized but the URC is delayed until an already opened socket is closed. If the listening queue is full, the TCP server ignores incoming connection requests, which may lead to a later attempt by the client.

18.25.1. Description

Starts the heartbeat service for the specified client.

The heartbeat service sends periodic heartbeat messages to the configured server and waits for a message response. If a message matching the one set arrives, the service wakes up the module from low power idle mode (see +UPSV) and can optionally activate a GPIO pin to trigger an action on an external device monitoring the GPIO.

Specifies the client link number.

The allowed range is 0-2.

<cause>

Number

Reason for unexpected link closure:

  • 1: remote closure.

  • 2: closure for other reasons.

18.26.4. Notes

  • The set command responds with 'OK' even if the service is not running.

18.27.3. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<link_num>

Number

Specifies the client link number.

The allowed range is 0-2.

<op_code>

String

Heartbeat parameter to configure:

  • "heartbeat_msg": set the message sent as heartbeat to the server

  • "wakeup_msg": set the message that the module waits for to wake up from power saving mode

  • "ignore_msg": set the message for which the module will not activate wake-up from power saving mode

  • "interrupt": set the handling of a GPIO when waking up the module from power saving mode

  • "gpio_num": set the pin number of the GPIO to pull

  • "gpio_level": set the level to set the GPIO pin to (0 or 1)

  • "gpio_time": set the duration to keep the GPIO pin at the specified level (in milliseconds)

  • "ssl_index": reserved; not for use

  • "autostop": set the automatic stopping of the heartbeat message sending after receiving the wake-up message

  • "retries": set the number of the heartbeat retransmissions before stopping the connection

  • "bind": set the already opened socket the heartbeat service binds to

  • "reconnect": reserved; not for use

<input_mode>

Number

Parameter value input mode; specifies how the <op_value> parameter is provided:

  • 0: the <op_value> parameter is provided as an ASCII string

  • 1: the <op_value> parameter is provided in binary syntax mode

  • 2: the <op_value> parameter is provided as a hexadecimal string

The <input_mode> values 1 and 2 are valid only when the <op_code> parameter is set to "heartbeat_msg", "wakeup_msg" or "ignore_msg".

<hb_msg>

String

The string message sent periodically to the server.

<wakeup_msg>

String

The string message received from the server the heartbeat service uses to exit power-saving mode.

<ignore_msg>

String

The string message received from the server ignored by the heartbeat service.

<interrupt>

Number

Enable the handling of a GPIO when the module wakes up from power-saving mode.

  • 0: (default) GPIO handling is disabled;

  • 1: GPIO handling is enabled.

<gpio_id>

Number

GPIO pin identifier: pin number

See the GPIO mapping for the available GPIO pins, their mapping and factory-programmed values on different cellular modules series and product version.

The GPIO pin must be already configured as output with the appropriate level by the +UGPIOC AT command.

<level>

Number

GPIO output value:

  • 0 (default): low

  • 1: high

<time>

Number

The time the GPIO pin is pulled, in milliseconds.

The allowed range is 0-5000.

The default value is 60.

<ssl_ctx_index>

Number

Reserved; not for use

The parameter is present to be compatible with old commands set.

<autostop>

Number

Configure automatic stopping of heartbeat message sending after receiving the wake-up message:

  • 0: (default) the auto stop mode is disabled;

  • 1: the auto stop mode is enabled.

<retry_num>

Number

The number of attempts to retransmit the heartbeat packet.

The allowed range is 0-12.

The default value is 6.

<socket>

Number

The socket index the heartbeat service binds to. Refer to the <socket> parameter of +USOPEN AT command

The socket must be already opened by the +USOPEN AT command.

The allowed range is 0-9.

The default value is -1.

The default value (-1) means that the heartbeat service is not bound to any socket opened by the +USOPEN AT command.

<reconnect_data>

Number

Reserved; not for use

The parameter is present to be compatible with old commands set.

18.27.4. Notes

  • If the <wakeup_msg> parameter is configured, the <ignore_msg> parameter does not take effect.

  • If the <ignore_msg> parameter is configured and the <wakeup_msg> parameter is not configured, the heartbeat application wakes the module up receiving any data except the <ignore_msg> message.

  • By configuring the parameters <hb_msg>, <wakeup_msg> or <ignore_msg> with the parameter <input_mode> set to 1 (binary syntax mode), the symbol ‘>’ is printed waiting for the corresponding string to be entered. The entry is terminated by sending the character <CTRL-Z>. If the command timeout (9 seconds) expires before the character <CTRL-Z> is sent, the command fails with the error +CME ERROR: 151 (AT command timeout) and to return to AT command mode, the user must still send the character <CTRL-Z>.

  • To restart sending the heartbeat messages after receiving the wakeup message when the <autostop> option is enabled, the heartbeat application must be stopped (+HBSTOP) and started (+HBSTART) again.

  • If the HB service is configured to be bound to a <socket> using the “bind” operating code, all URCs relating to the socket are sent once the GPIO management operations have been completed, when enabled. For example, the +IPD URC, when the socket is configured in Direct Push Access mode (+USGET=0), or the +USGET URC when the socket is configured in Buffer Access mode (+USGET=1), are sent to the AT terminal after the GPIO line has returned to its default value, when a received message triggers the device to wake up.

18.28. Secure data reporting mode +USECREP

+USECREP

Modules

All products

Attributes

Syntax

PIN required

Settings saved

Response time

Error reference

Full

No

No

No

120000 ms

Secure error code

18.28.1. Description

Configures the reporting mode for data sent and received respectively with +USECSEND and +USECREAD AT commands:

  • Sent data report

    • <report_send_result>=0 : (default mode) after sending data with +USECSEND, no URC will be reported.

    • <report_send_result>=1 : when sending data is complete, the +USECSEND URC will be reported.

  • Received data report

    • <recv_mode>=0 : Direct Push mode, the data from remote host is directly outputted to the terminal by an URC with DATA indication, <session_id> and the data lenght.

    • <recv_mode>=1 : Buffer Access mode, the received data are buffered and a "+: <session_id>,RECV EVENT" URC is notified. The data can be received using +USECREAD AT command.

The command must be called before +USECSTART

18.28.2. Syntax

Type Syntax Response Example

Generic syntax

Set

AT+USECREP=<report_send_result>,<recv_mode>

[OK|ERROR]

AT+USECREP=0,1

OK

Read

AT+USECREP?

+USECREP: <report_send_result>,<recv_mode>

OK

AT+USECREP?

+USECREP: 0,1

OK

Test

AT+USECREP=?

+USECREP: (<report_send_result>'s range),(<recv_mode>'s range)

OK

+USECREP: (0,1),(0,1)

OK

18.28.3. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<report_send_result>

Number

Set how to report the result of +USECSEND AT command:

  • 0: (default value) no URC will be returned

  • 1: the URC +USECSEND will be sent when sending data has completed

<recv_mode>

Number

Set how received data will be shown:

  • 0: (default value) data is outputted after URC +USECREAD

  • 1: the URC +CCHEVENT will be displayed when new data is ready to be read

18.29. Direct Link TLS/DTLS connection mode +USECMODE

+USECMODE

Modules

All products

Attributes

Syntax

PIN required

Settings saved

Can be aborted

Response time

Error reference

Full

No

No

No

120000 ms

-

18.29.1. Description

Establishes a direct link end-to-end communication by connecting a TLS/DTLS socket to a remote host via the serial interface. The data can be sent to the TLS/DTLS socket and can be received via the serial interface: HW flow control usage is strongly recommended to avoid data loss.

The direct link TLS/DTLS connection mode can be exited via the +++ sequence or via the DTR line transition according the &D configuration. The socket will remain connected and communication can be re-established any time by the ATO command.

Only TLS/DTLS secure socket session 0 (session ID = 0) can be set into direct link mode. See +USECOPEN command.

The command must be called before +USECSTART

When exiting direct link mode using either +++ or a DTR line transition, it is not possible to send or receive data using +USECSEND or +USECREAD and no URCs will be reported for incoming data. Any new data received will be buffered and delivered to the serial interface once the direct link is re-established using the ATO AT command.

18.29.2. Syntax

Type Syntax Response Example

Generic syntax

Set

AT+USECMODE=<mode>

[OK|ERROR]

OK

OK

+USECMODE: 1

OK

Test

+USECMODE: (<mode>'s range)

OK

+USECMODE: (0,1)

OK

<mode>

Number

Enable the direct link mode

  • 0: (default value) command mode

  • 1: direct link mode

18.30.1. Description

Starts the secure socket service and activates the associated PDP context if not already active. The command must be performed before executing any other TLS/DTLS service operation. A specific PDP context can be activated providing the <cid> parameter.

If the PDP context is deactivated (e.g. registration failure, mobile-originated or mobile terminated LTE detach), the "+CCH: CCH STOP" URC is provided. When this event happens, the opened secure sockets will be closed. When the AT+USECSTART=<cid> command is used to activate a PDP context, the URC carries the <cid> parameter, and a URC is issued for each deactivated <cid>.

Number

For more details on the default value of the parameter (where supported), see Internet protocol transport layer.

If neither <session_id> nor <cid> is set, the cid of all sessions are queried, If <cid> is not set, the cid of the current session is queried, and the default value of cid is 1.

18.37.1. Description

Reads the data received from the remote TCP/TLS or UDP/DTLS server. Data can be received in two modes, depending on <recv_mode> of +USECREP setting:

  • 0: Direct Push mode;

  • 1: Buffer Access mode.

In case of Direct Push mode, all received data is displayed by the URC; in case of Buffer Access mode, a specific URC notifies the occurrence of data reception event and data can be read from the buffer with the set command.

The command must be called after +USECSTART and +USECOPEN

19. Device and data security

19.1. Introduction

Nowadays the security is very important to secure personal or confidential data from unauthorized access and therefore it is important to secure the IoT devices to protect the business and the data.

In the IoT security, a weak point is a defect which is called a vulnerability and it may become a safety issue; IoT devices connects/links physical objects and so in IoT it is needed to secure of course data traffic and networks but also the network of "things" or physical objects (i.e. medical devices, infrastructure, utility meters, vehicles, etc.) must be secured.

Some definitions are needed to understand the foundations of security:

  • Integrity is about making sure that some pieces of data have not been altered from some "reference version".

  • Authentication is about making sure that a given entity (with whom you are interacting) is who the user believes it to be.

  • Authenticity is a special case of integrity, where the "reference version" is defined as "whatever it was when it was under control of a specific entity".

  • Confidentiality means no unauthorized access to data (i.e. encryption/cryptography).

Our security solution secures the IoT devices from end-to-end:

  • Device security, the privacy of data is protected from the devices to the cloud (confidentiality, integrity and authenticity).

  • Data security, the devices are protected from attack, they can be trusted and controlled (identity, authenticity and firmware protection).

  • Access Management, it can be controlled who has access to data and products (device policies, data policies and feature authorization)

The pillars of the this security are:

  • Unique device identity, an immutable chip ID and a robust Root-of-Trust (RoT) provides the foundational security.

  • Secure boot sequence and updates, only authenticated and authorized firmware and updates can run on the device.

  • Hardware-backed crypto functions, a Secure Client Library (SCL) generates keys and crypto functions to securely connect to the cloud.

The IoT device is secured through different steps:

  • Provision trust: insert Root-of-Trust at production. An immutable chip ID and hardware-based Root-of-Trust provide foundational security and a unique device identity.

  • Leverage trust: derive trusted keys. Secure libraries allow generation of hardware-backed crypto functions and keys that securely connect to the cloud.

  • Guarantee trust: use keys to secure any function. It ensures authenticity, integrity, and confidentiality to maintain control of device and data.

19.2. Data security provided by secure connections (SSL/TLS/DTLS)

19.2.1. Introduction

SSL/TLS/DTLS (where supported) provides a secure connection between two entities using TCP/UDP or UDP/DTLS socket for communication (i.e. HTTP/FTP server and HTTP/FTP client).

The SSL/TLS/DTLS with digital certificates support provides different connection security aspects:

  • Server authentication: use of the server certificate verification against a specific trusted certificate or a trusted certificates list;

  • Client authentication: use of the client certificate and the corresponding private key;

  • Data security and integrity: data encryption and Hash Message Authentication Code (HMAC) generation.

The security aspects used in the current connection depend on the SSL/TLS/DTLS configuration and features supported by the communicating entities.

The cellular modules support all the described aspects of SSL/TLS/DTLS security protocol with these AT commands:

  • AT+UCERTDWNL, AT+CCERTMOVE, AT+UCERTLIST, AT+UCERTDELETE : import, removal, list and information retrieval of certificates or private keys that are stored as file in secure repository and retrieved by TLS/DTLS layer as configured;

  • AT+USSLCFG: configuration of Secure context profiles used for an TLS/DTLS connection.

The USSLCFG provides a default TLS/DTLS profile which cannot be modified. The default USSLCFG profile provides the following TLS/DTLS settings:

Setting Value Meaning

Minimum SSL/TLS/DTLS version

both TLS1.3 or TLS1.2

The server can use any of the TLS1.2/TLS1.3 or DTLS1.2 versions for the connection.

Certificates validation level

Level 0

The server certificate will not be checked or verified.

Local Time certificate check

Disabled

The server certificate validation date will not be checked.

Negotiation Time

300

Timeout of TLS handshake

Trusted root certificate internal name

"" (none)

No certificate will be used for the server authentication.

Client certificate internal name

"" (none)

No client certificate will be used.

Client private key internal name

"" (none)

No client private key will be used.

Client private key password

"" (none)

No client private key password will be used.

Server Name Indication (SNI)

0

No SNI.

Server certificate Common Name (CN) check

0 (none)

No check for server certificate Common Name.

DTLS Client Hello repetition

9

Up to 9 retransmissions of the DTLS ClientHello in case of no server response.

For the configuration of the settings listed above, see the +USSLCFG AT command.

Secure repository can handle certificate/key/password filenames in ASCII and HTML encoded UTF-8 characters. If the filename must be saved in HTML encoded UTF-8, its filename must have the prefix {non-ascii}, followed by its name, with .pem or .der extension between "". The string between "" must to be decoded in hex value. For example:, if the filename is in: UTF-8 notation : U+4444 HTML encoded UTF-8 notation : 䑄 , then the filename used in the AT command needs to be {non-ascii}"262378343434343B2E70656D"

Parameter Type Description

<filename>

String

The name of the certificate/key/password file. The file can only have these extensions: '.pem' or '.der'. If the filename contains any characters that are not valid ASCII, encode the entire filename (including the extension) as a hexadecimal string of its original byte sequence (HTML encoded UTF-8 characters), enclose it in double quotes, and prefix it with {non-ascii}, see AT command setting. 19.8.1. Description

Manages security profiles for the configuration of the following TLS/DTLS connections properties:

  • Authentication mode / Certificate validation level

  • TLS/DTLS version to be used

    • The configured version should be supported by the server: if the version supported by the server is unknowns, use the default value.

  • Certificate expiration date handling

  • TLS handshake timeout

  • Certificates\keys\passwords used during TLS/DTLS handshake

    • The root CA of the server, the certificate and the key of the client can be imported with the +UCERTDWNL or +CCERTMOVE AT commands.

  • SNI (Server Name Indication)

    • SNI is a feature of TLS/DTLS which uses an additional TLS/DTLS extension header to specify the server name to which the client is connecting to. The extension was introduced to support the certificate handling used with virtual hosting provided by the various TLS/DTLS enabled servers mostly in cloud based infrastructures. With the SNI a server has the opportunity to present a different server certificate (or/and whole TLS/DTLS configuration) based on the host indicated by the SNI extension. When SNI is not used the modules might receive a non-host specific TLS/DTLS configuration (version/cipher suites/certificate) when used with virtual hosts. The SNI feature is always enabled, the parameter <enableSNI_flag> has no effect.

  • Common Name handling

  • Cipher Suites

    • Cipher suites define the cryptographic algorithms used in a TLS/DTLS session (key exchange, encryption, integrity). The client advertises an ordered list of supported cipher suites in the ClientHello, and the server selects one from that list. This list is not configurable via AT commands. The module uses predefined cipher-suite sets depending on the selected mode: DTLS 1.2 only, TLS 1.2 only, TLS 1.3 only, or TLS 1.3 with fallback to TLS 1.2. The tables below list the cipher suites included in each of these four cases.

  • DTLS Client Hello repetitions

  • Session recovery

    • Session ID available for TLS 1.2 only (<session_cache>=1 and <sslversion>=0).

    • Session ticket available for TLS 1.2 only (<session_cache>=1, <use_ticket>=1 and <sslversion>=0).

    • PSK ticket available for TLS 1.3 only (<session_cache>=1, <use_ticket>=1 and <sslversion>=1).

TLS_EMPTY_RENEGOTIATION_INFO_SCSV

TLS_EMPTY_RENEGOTIATION_INFO_SCSV (0x00FF) is included to signal secure renegotiation support. It is not a cipher suite and cannot be used for data encryption.

If a DTLS secure context is defined (with AT+USSLCFG="sslversion",<ssl_ctx_index>,12), a TCP/IP application will establish a TLS1.2 connection to the server.

19.8.3. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<op_string>

String

Operational string:

  • "sslversion" - set the TLS/DTLS client version

  • "authmode" - set the authentication mode

  • "ignorelocaltime" - set the ignore local time check flag

  • "negotiatetime" - set the Handshake negotiation time

  • "cacert" - set CA certificate file name

  • "clientcert" - set the Client certificate file name

  • "clientkey" - set the Client key file name

  • "password" - set the password file name

  • "enableSNI" - set the SNI enable flag

  • "ignorecertCN" - set the ignore server certificate common name check flag

  • "dtlsnegotiateretry" - set the number of DTLS Client Hello repetitions

  • "session_cache" - enable TLS session caching

  • "use_tickets" - enable TLS session ticket or PSK ticket

<ssl_ctx_index>

Number

TLS/DTLS secure context ID. The range is 0-9.

<sslversion>

Number

The client TLS/DTLS version:

  • 0: TLS1.2

  • 1: TLS1.3

  • 2: all TLS (default)

  • 12: DTLS1.2

The configured version should be support by the server. It is recommended to use the default value if the TLS version supported by the server is unknown.

<authmode>

Number

The authentication mode

  • 0: no authentication (default).

  • 1: server authentication. It needs the root CA of the server.

  • 2: server and client authentication. It needs the root CA of the server, the certificate and the key of the client. If the server does not need to authenticate the client, it is equivalent to value 1.

  • 3: client authentication and no server authentication. It needs the certificate and the key of the client. If the server does not need to authenticate the client, it is equivalent to value 0.

<ignoreltime>

Number

The flag to indicate how to deal with expired certificates:

  • 0: consider time check for certification.

  • 1: ignore time check for certification (default).

When the value is set to 0, current date and time shall be configured in the module (see +CCLK) when using SSL certification.

<negotiatetime>

Number

The timeout value used in TLS negotiate stage. The range is 10-300 seconds. The default value is 300. It takes effect only for TLS connection.

<ca_file>

String

The root CA file name of the TLS/DTLS context. The file can only have these extensions: '.pem' or '.der'. If the filename contains any characters that are not valid ASCII, encode the entire filename (including the extension) as a hexadecimal string of its original byte sequence (HTML encoded UTF-8 characters), enclose it in double quotes, and prefix it with {non-ascii}, see AT command setting. The length of <filename> goes from 5 to 108 bytes including {non-ascii} and "" if not UTF-8 characters.

<clientcert_file>

String

The client certificate file name of the TLS/DTLS context. The file can only have these extensions: '.pem' or '.der'. If the filename contains any characters that are not valid ASCII, encode the entire filename (including the extension) as a hexadecimal string of its original byte sequence (HTML encoded UTF-8 characters), enclose it in double quotes, and prefix it with {non-ascii}, see AT command setting. The length of <filename> goes from 5 to 108 bytes including {non-ascii} and "" if not UTF-8 characters.

<clientkey_file>

String

The client key file name of the TLS/DTLS context. The file can only have these extensions: '.pem' or '.der'. If the filename contains any characters that are not valid ASCII, encode the entire filename (including the extension) as a hexadecimal string of its original byte sequence (HTML encoded UTF-8 characters), enclose it in double quotes, and prefix it with {non-ascii}, see AT command setting. The length of <filename> goes from 5 to 108 bytes including {non-ascii} and "" if not UTF-8 characters.

<password_file>

String

The password file name of the TLS/DTLS context used to decrypt the client key. The file can only have these extensions: '.pem' or '.der'. If the filename contains any characters that are not valid ASCII, encode the entire filename (including the extension) as a hexadecimal string of its original byte sequence (HTML encoded UTF-8 characters), enclose it in double quotes, and prefix it with {non-ascii}, see AT command setting. The length of <filename> goes from 5 to 108 bytes including {non-ascii} and "" if not UTF-8 characters.

<enableSNI_flag>

Number

The flag to enable/disable the SNI.

  • 0: SNI not enabled. (default)

  • 1: SNI enabled.

<ignorecertCN_flag>

Number

The flag to enable/disable the server certificate common name verification.

  • 0: CN verification disabled (default).

  • 1: CN verification enabled.

<dtlsnegotiateretry>

Number

The number of DTLS Client Hello repetitions. The range is 0-9. The default value is 9.

<session_cache>

Number

The flag to enable/disable TLS session caching.

  • 0: TLS session caching disabled. (default)

  • 1: TLS session caching enabled.

<use_tickets>

Number

The flag to enable/disable TLS Session ticket/PSK.

  • 0: Session ticket or PSK ticket disabled. (default)

  • 1: Session ticket or PSK ticket enabled.

20. FTP

Proprietary AT commands. FTP AT commands set can be used for sending and receiving files over the available bearer, transparently retrieving and storing them in the file system. Standard file and directory management operations on the remote FTP server are as well possible. The FTP client requires an active connection to work. Some products require additional commands to provide connectivity to the application.

If not specified, the default CID (<cid>=1) is used. If not specified and the protocol type is IPv4v6, then the preferred protocol type is IPv4.

See +CGACT AT command for activating a PDP context.

  • The UFTP commands are available only after +UFTPSTART command is entered. It will be possible to use these commands until +UFTPSTOP is issued.

  • The +UFTPLOGIN command starts a FTP session by connecting to a remote FTP server. The +UFTPLOGOUT command terminates the FTP session. Only one session at a time can be activated.

  • Commands that interact with the FTP server (i.e. +UFTPSTART, +UFTPLOGIN, etc) notify the final result via a specific URC. The following UFTP commands shall be entered after receiving the URC. For more detailed description, refer to the Syntax section of each UFTP command.

20.1. FTP init +UFTPSTART

+UFTPSTART

Modules

All products

Attributes

Syntax

PIN required

Settings saved

Can be aborted

Response time

Error reference

Full

Yes

No

No

< 9 s

Error codes

20.1.1. Description

Allocates the configuration resources, starts the FTP service and allows to use the UFTP commands. This command should be entered before any other UFTP command otherwise an error will be reported. UFTP commands are available until +UFTPSTOP is issued.

FTP will use an activated PDN context that can be selected as parameter. Context should be previously configured using +CGDCONT command and activated via +CGACT.

20.1.2. Syntax

Type Syntax Response Example

Action

AT+UFTPSTART

OK or ERROR

[+UFTPSTART: <result>]

AT+UFTPSTART

OK

+UFTPSTART: 0

Set

AT+UFTPSTART=<cid>

OK or ERROR

[+UFTPSTART: <result>,<cid>]

AT+UFTPSTART=1

OK

+UFTPSTART: 0,1

AT+UFTPSTART=30

ERROR

Test

AT+UFTPSTART=?

+UFTPSTART: (list of supported <cid>s)

OK

AT+UFTPSTART=?

+UFTPSTART: (1-n)

OK

URC

+UFTPSTART: <result>[,<cid>]

+UFTPSTART: 0

20.1.3. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<cid>

Number

Specifies the PDP context that will be used for the FTP data. For the parameter range, see <cid>. For more details on the default value of the parameter (where supported), see FTP.

<result>

Number

Result code of the command:

  • 0: success;

  • other values: failure, see FTP error codes

20.1.4. Notes

  • The command returns ERROR if the FTP service has been already activated.

20.2.1. Description

Terminates the FTP service and releases the configuration resources. After this command any further UFTP command will return ERROR until a new +UFTPSTART is issued. The FTP session should be disconnected (see +UFTPLOGOUT) before terminating the FTP service: +UFTPSTOP returns ERROR if the session is active.

Connects to a FTP server and starts a FTP session. It should be called after the +UFTPSTART command. Only one session at a time can be activated.

Type Syntax Response Example

Set

OK or ERROR

[+UFTPLOGIN: <result>]

AT+UFTPLOGIN="ftp.server.com",21,"user","pass",0

OK

+UFTPLOGIN: 0

AT+UFTPLOGIN="ftp.server.com",990,"user","pass"

OK

+UFTPLOGIN: 13

OK

+UFTPLOGIN: 1

OK

OK

AT+UFTPLOGIN=?

URC

+UFTPLOGIN: <result>

+UFTPLOGIN: 0

20.5.3. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<server_name>

String

FTP server name (e.g. "ftp.server.com"). The maximum length is 128 characters.

<ftp_port>

Number

Remote FTP server listening port; it must be a valid TCP port value. The value is in [1-65535] range.

<username>

String

User name (the maximum length is 128 characters) for the FTP login procedure.

<password>

String

Password (the maximum length is 128 characters) for the FTP login procedure.

<server_type>

Number

Type of FTP server. Allowed values are:

  • 0: default: FTP server

  • 2: FTPS server with TLS authentication

<ftp_status>

Number

FTP login status:

  • 0: logged out

  • 1: logged in

<result>

Number

Result code of the command request:

  • 0: success;

  • other values: failure, see FTP error codes

20.5.4. Notes

  • When successful login on FTP server is perfomed, it will be necessary to use command +UFTPLOGOUT before stopping the FTP service with command +UFTPLSTOP otherwise it will report ERROR.

20.17.1. Description

Sends a file to the FTP server using the direct link. The command handler activates a serial interface, switches to serial mode and waits for the data. The ">" indicates the user to input the file content.

The command interface returns to normal mode when sent data reaches the length specified in the command (<data_len>) or when <Ctrl+Z> (0x1A) is entered.

20.17.2. Syntax

Type Syntax Response Example

Set

AT+UFTPPUT=<file_path>[,<data_len>[,<rest_size>]]

In case of success

>

…​ data …​

OK

+UFTPPUT: 0

In case of failure

OK or ERROR

[+UFTPPUT: <result>]

AT+UFTPPUT="testfile",12

>

Hello world!

OK

+UFTPPUT: 0

AT+UFTPPUT="file.txt",1250,200

OK

+UFTPPUT: 9

Test

AT+UFTPPUT=?

+UFTPPUT: "FILEPATH"[,<data_len>[,<rest_size>]]

OK

AT+UFTPPUT=?

+UFTPPUT: "FILEPATH"[,<data_len>[,<rest_size>]]

OK

20.17.3. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<file_path>

String

Remote file path on the FTP server. Maximum allowed length is 112 chars.

<data_len>

Number

Length of data to send. Maximum value is 2048 bytes.

If parameter <data_len> is omitted,

  • A single <Ctrl+Z> (0x1A) ends the data input and the direct link mode.

  • The <ETX> (0x03) is the escape character to be used for coding all the <Ctrl+Z> characters present in the data flow: <ETX><Ctrl+Z> (0x031A).

  • The <ETX> (0x03) is also the escape character to be used for coding all the <ETX> characters present in the data flow: <ETX><ETX> (0x0303).

<ETX> is decoded as 0x03, and <Ctrl+Z> is decoded as 0x1A.

<rest_size>

Number

Offset in the file to start uploading. It is the number of bytes to offset from the beginning of the remote file.

The range goes from 0 to 2147483647 bytes, the default value is 0.

<result>

Number

Result code of the command:

  • 0: success;

  • other values: failure, see FTP Error codes

20.18. FTP URC errors

The following URC notifies the user that the current UFTP session is lost.

20.18.1. Syntax

Syntax Example

Passive disconnection

+UFTPCONNLOST: <cid>,<cause>

+UFTPCONNLOST: 1,3

Network disconnection

+UFTPNONET

+UFTPNONET

20.18.2. Defined values

Parameter Type Description

<cid>

Number

PDP context identifier. The allowed range is product specific, see <cid>.

<cause>

Number

The cause of disconnection:

  • 1: Socket passively closed

  • 2: Socket reset

  • 3: Network disconnection

21. HTTP

The section describes the proprietary AT commands for sending requests to a remote HTTP server, receiving the server response, and transparently storing it in the file system. The supported methods are: HEAD, GET, DELETE, PUT, POST file and POST data. The HTTP client requires an active connection to work. Some products require additional commands to provide connectivity to the application.

If not specified, the default CID (<cid>=1) is used. If not specified and the protocol type is IPv4v6, then the preferred protocol type is IPv4.

See +CGACT AT command for activating a PDP context.

There is only a profile allowed for any HTTP operation that will not be specified in commands.

The UHTTP commands are available only after +UHTTPSTART command is entered. It will be possible to use these commands until +UHTTPSTOP is issued.

Commands that interact with the HTTP server (i.e. +UHTTPSTART, +UHTTPACT, etc) notify the final result via a specific URC. The following UHTTP commands shall be entered after receiving the URC. For more detailed description, refer to the Syntax section of each UHTTP command.
